current_status.from: Partially superseded as of 2026-09-14. Colleton County Council unanimously adopted (third reading) a Digital Infrastructure Overlay District ordinance permitting data centers and battery energy storage systems, subject to conditions (300+ acre minimum, 65 dB noise cap, 200-ft buffers, closed-loop cooling), west of Interstate 95 and on land already zoned Light/Industrial/Industrial/Heavy Industrial; the moratorium (Ordinance 26-O-04) is repealed with respect to those areas but continues to apply elsewhere in the county (east of I-95, non-industrial-zoned land) through its original ~180-day term (adopted 2026-07-06, running to approximately 2027-01-02) absent further council action.
current_status.to: On September 14, 2026, Ordinance 26-O-08 partially repealed the moratorium for areas west of I-95 and areas zoned LID, ID or HID; it states that the moratorium remains in effect east of I-95 outside those industrial zones until final approval of the specified comprehensive-plan update. Later actions and current force require further review. outcome.from: Adopted six-month moratorium in July 2026 (Ordinance 26-O-04); on 2026-09-14 the county partially repealed that moratorium and replaced it, for areas west of I-95 and already-industrial-zoned land, with a Digital Infrastructure Overlay District permitting data centers and battery storage under conditions (minimum 300 acres, 65 dB noise cap, 200-ft buffers, closed-loop cooling); the moratorium remains in force elsewhere in the county pending its original term.
